column3: Zero-shot generation of a bare Pod. Explicit negative scope ("do not add anything else") keeps the output identical to the specification instead of letting the model "improve" it.
HTTP liveness probe. The prompt names the reason for a design choice (probe on the named port so it cannot drift from the container port), which steers the model away from the bug in the original.
Structured input: the specification is given as key-value lines, so every probe parameter maps 1:1 to a field and nothing is left to the model's defaults.
Pod with probes and a hostPath volume. Exact volume type (DirectoryOrCreate) is part of the instruction, so creating a missing node directory is explicit instead of left to the untyped default.

CronJob on the current batch/v1 API. Behaviour is described in plain words ("must not start while the previous one is still running") and the model translates it into concurrencyPolicy and history limits.

Contextual prompting: the pipeline is described step by step (sync bucket, then process) and the deprecated in-tree GCE disk is replaced by a PersistentVolumeClaim. No lifecycle hooks, because preStop never fires for a run-to-completion container.
Pattern-oriented prompt: names the sidecar content-generator pattern and the role of each container, with pinned image tags.
Compute resources with exact requests and limits next to the probes; numbers are given, not left to the model.
Pod that reads credentials via secretKeyRef. One manifest per file: the prompt names the dependency (Secret in app-secret.yaml) and excludes it, so the file stays a single YAML document.
The Secret the app-secret-env Pod depends on, as its own manifest, with placeholder values instead of real credentials.
Ingress for the optional Gateway API part: ingressClassName nginx and standard fields only, so ingress2gateway can convert it without losing controller-specific annotations.
Review of a bare Pod against production expectations (self-healing, health checks, resources, security context), with the constraint to keep image, labels and port.
Symptom-first context ("restarts every ~30 seconds"): the model is asked for the root cause before other findings. Finds the probe port 8000 vs container port 8080 mismatch.
Consistency check between the two probes, the container port and the probe timings.
Review from the perspective of a multi-tenant platform team: storage choice (hostPath) and its security and scheduling consequences come first.
Failure-driven context ("applying to 1.34 fails"): the model explains the removed batch/v1beta1 API, fixes it, then checks overlapping runs, history limits and the untagged image.

Debugging a reported symptom ("preStop never writes its message"), then a review of volume types and image tag. The answer is capped at 3 findings: the full review did not fit into kubectl-ai's output length.
Review of a two-container Pod: naming, image pinning and resource limits for both containers.
Assessment prompt that explicitly allows "nothing is broken": request/limit ratio and the resulting QoS class.
Secret handling: what happens when the referenced Secret is missing, plus image pinning and secret-handling security.
